The patient's electrocardiogram shows regular narrow complex tachycardia with visible P waves, consistent with orthodromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia.
The patient has a history of Fontan circulation and presents with lightheadedness and syncope, suggesting a complication related to the Fontan circulation.
The patient's persistent tachycardia and palpitations may be causing cardiomyopathy.

It explains the uncovered findings of D-transposition of the great arteries and large ventricular septal defect with outflow extension, which are risk factors for this condition.
